title: Harvey for Outlook: Draft, Summarize, and Respond with AI
format_note: Silent-narration music-only walkthrough: phone prompt, drafted email, then Outlook side panel, closing on a Microsoft partnership lockup and Coming Soon.
one_thing: Harvey's AI drafts and edits a legal email inside Outlook, and it is coming soon.

transcript.voice_style: No voice. Whisper output was the typed prompt text plus a hallucinated Thank you; the film is music only.
transcript.script_shape: All copy is on screen: tagline, a typed user prompt, UI text, partner lockup, Coming Soon, closing line. Story told by product UI, not captions.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: One hard cut at 3.0 s, then one 37 s shot in which a single UI object resizes, dissolves and morphs into the next scene. Scene changes land about every 3 to 8 s, with static stretches up to 10 s (intervals_static_share 0.579).

good.observation: The product story is one continuous object transformation (card to phone to Outlook window to Send button to logo lockup), so one scene hands off to the next with no hard cuts after 3 s.
The film is calm and sparse: one subject at a time on a flat off-white ground, with only the product's purple and Outlook blue as colour.
The typed prompt is real copy a lawyer would write, and the Make this email more concise follow-up shows a second action, so the capability is demonstrated rather than named.
The Send button becomes the Harvey / Microsoft lockup, giving a causal, on-screen reason for the partner reveal.
Closing hold is long and still: AI Tailored for Law sits unchanged for about 4 s.

rule_candidates.rule: A single UI object can carry the whole film: scale, dissolve or morph it into the next view instead of cutting. The film has one hard cut in 40 s and still reads as paced.
For a minimal calm film the median shot may exceed 3.5 s if something on screen changes at least every 8 s; a 20 s shot works when the object keeps transforming.
Show the product's real action in two steps: a typed prompt and a follow-up edit prompt, so the viewer sees what the tool does rather than a label.
Make the brand or partner lockup an effect of the last UI action, for example a Send button that morphs into the logo, rather than a new slide.
Titles in a sparse serif film can sit at 7 to 9 % of frame height centred on a flat ground; measured 6.9, 8.9, 7.1, 7.1 %.
After a wide window shot, zoom to the panel in use within 2 s so text exceeds 2.6 % of height; full-window text was about 1.3 %.
Close with the status line as a static hold of about 4 s: Coming Soon then AI Tailored for Law; measured hold 4.1 s on the last title.
Do not rely on a music bed unlocked from picture for a sync claim: with one cut and 0.0 share on onsets, measure the music peak against the hero moment before adding sound.
